newsitem.title: CONGO: Loss of oil accounts hits Congo state assurer.
newsitem.headline: Loss of oil accounts hits Congo state assurer.

text.p: State-owned Congo Insurance and Reassurance (ARC) has lost 40 percent of annual turnover since the start of 1996 after oil companies moved their weighty accounts from the firm, an official source said on Tuesday.
Oil producing firms led by France's Elf-Aquitaine moved their accounts to the Conogelese Assurance and Insurance Co after it was created last February.

The source said the move translated into a loss of about 2.5 billion CFA francs of ARC's annual revenues. Industry sources said the oil companies jumped for a chance to deal with a privately-owned insurance firm.

ARC, which is one of the state firms scheduled for privatisation in the Central African country, monopolised Congo's reassurance market until the liberalisation of the insurance sector early last year.

Its annual turnover in 1994 was 6.5 billion CFA, most of it (5.9 billion CFA) from fire, accidents and other risks policies, while life insurance and capitalisation accounted for 43.5 million CFA. There were no revenue figures for 1995 and 1996.
Conogelese Assurance and Insurance Co is majority-owned by foreign interests, notably French, with the state holding a 35 percent stake.

It was established in March 1995 following reforms that opened up the sector. Liberalisation led to rapid growth of the industry, which experts say has potential of generating turnover of 15 to 20 billion CFA yearly.
